title: Webhook ingestion and verification
subtitle: Inbound vendor events are signature-checked, batched durably and delivered to the team that caused them, in the gateway and in the in-house social integrations.

stats.label: replay window on every signed delivery
attempts at most, at widening intervals, on network and server errors only
between checks for events left unanswered past their deadline

lede: FAFOHive receives webhooks in two event planes, and I set the same three rules for both: check the signature over the untouched body, store before acknowledging, and keep event redelivery separate from action repetition. Signatures are checked over raw bytes, because re-serialised JSON no longer matches. Events may be redelivered; payment and social actions are never repeated. The platforms define their webhook formats; the receivers, the shared contract, the listener and the delivery semantics are mine. FAFO Core and Function Forge has a sibling platform that puts third-party APIs behind generic MCP servers, and webhook ingestion keeps its local copy of each vendor's data current between calls.
quote: An unanswered event escalates on a timer, so "answer every customer" is something the system checks.
evidence: Webhook ingestion and verification: signatures checked over the raw body before parsing, events stored before acknowledging, redelivery kept apart from action repetition.
Message signing and replay protection: a shared HMAC contract with a 300 s replay window and two secret slots for rotation.
Reliable delivery: retries at widening intervals up to 6 attempts on network and server errors only, and breach events every 5 min for anything unanswered past its deadline.
author: Corey James
